ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two large circles of radius 2 overlapping up and down, and a small circle of radius 1 is located in the middle of their common part. The upper and lower endpoints of the small circle are labeled B and A, and AB is a diameter of the small circle. The figure also shows that B is the center of the upper large circle, and A is the center of the lower large circle, so the distance between the centers of the two large circles of radius 2 is AB=2. The gray region represents the part inside the two large circles but outside the small circle. Then reason: The required region equals the overlapping lens area of two large circles of radius 2 with center distance 2, minus the area of the middle small circle of radius 1. The formula for the overlap area of two equal-radius circles is lens = 2R^2 arccos(d/(2R)) - (d/2)√(4R^2-d^2). Taking R=2, d=2, get lens = 2·4·arccos(2/4) - 1·√(16-4) = 8·arccos(1/2) - √12 = 8π/3 - 2√3. The area of the small circle is π, so the required area is 8π/3 - 2√3 - π = 5π/3 - 2√3.
